name: ready-gate
summary: Runtime code for the game itself: a loading gate that opens only when the world is ready to be seen, a spawn that never shows a character in bind pose, and captures of the first frames to prove both.
adapt: Let Unity create the .meta files (the next compile does it) and commit them with the scripts.
Start the game's loading flow with ReadyGate.Begin(cover) and put the game's own conditions behind it: player spawned and posed, camera placed, generated content done.
Replace Instantiate with Spawn.Posed for every animated character, and call Spawn.ShowWhenPosed when taking one from a pool.
Add the level's ShaderVariantCollection assets to gate.shaderWarmUp; without one there is nothing to warm up and first-use shader hitches remain.
Capture the first frames with FirstFrames.AfterGate and look at them before calling the loading flow done.
verify: node Tools/gam3/unity_run.mjs test --platform PlayMode --filter Gam3.Tests --profile agent

verified.how: Play-mode tests run in batch mode with unity_run.mjs under blind, agent and human: 10 tests in Gam3.Tests, all passed (the FirstFrames test is skipped under blind). They cover: the cover stays up while a hold is out and drops when the gate opens; conditions, a tracked AsyncOperation and settled frames; the timeout opens the gate and names what it waited for; FirstFrames writes one PNG per frame; a plain Instantiate in LateUpdate is measured in bind pose on its first visible frame (the control); Spawn.Posed is measured in the animated pose on that frame, also with a culled Animator; a pooled object restarts from the first frame; an object with no controller stays hidden until it has one, and is shown with a warning after giveUpSeconds. In the test project, three more tests (not shipped): the gate waited for a real additive async load of a terrain scene and the first frames after it were captured and looked at; a frame hitch restarted the settled count. Not run: a built player, the texture streaming wait and the shader warm-up step (the project had neither), URP, HDRP, a real skinned character (the rig is a generated one-bone Animator), Windows, Linux.
